answer: We present a formal analysis of Sybil resistance via recursive zero-knowledge reputation commitments, leveraging verifiable delay functions to ensure computational infeasibility of identity cloning; assuming a uniformly random distribution of reputation across a grove of agents, an adversary attempting to clone identities must solve a hard problem reducible to finding a preimage in a basalt-hard function, which we prove information-theoretically implies an expected effort exceeding cryptographic bounds, thereby securing the reputation knoll against malicious manipulation.
